messages.content: You check claims about a scientific paper against the evidence each one cites. A claim is supported only if the cited evidence says it AS WRITTEN: the same subject, row, column, setting and number. A correct value attached to the wrong subject or row is NOT supported, and neither is a claim that goes beyond its evidence. Judge only from the cited evidence; figure images are attached where a claim cites a figure. Give a verdict for every claim.

Claims:
1. "The knowledge gates are inspired by the powerful gate mechanism used in recurrent neural networks (RNN) to control information flow, and they are used to incorporate prior knowledge into the matching process." -- cites: E2 (Section abstract): quote "Knowledge Gate Inspired by the powerful gate mechanism (Hochreiter and Schmidhuber 1997; Chung et al. 2014) which controls information in and out when processing sequential data with recurrent neural networks (RNN), we propose using knowledge gates to incorporate prior knowledge into matching."
2. "The knowledge gates are used to filter out noise and highlight the useful information to matching in a piece of text." -- cites: E2 (Section abstract): quote "The underlying motivation is that we want to use the prior knowledge to filter out noise and highlight the useful information to matching in a piece of text."
3. "The knowledge gates are located in the KEHNN architecture as shown in Figure 1." -- cites: E4 (Figure 1): observation "Knowledge Gates are printed in the figure and are located in the KEHNN architecture."
4. "The role of the knowledge gates in the KEHNN architecture is to incorporate prior knowledge and filter out noise, as shown in the zoomed view of Figure 1." -- cites: E5 (Figure 1): observation "The zoomed view of Figure 1 shows the knowledge gates incorporated into the KEHNN architecture."

Cited evidence:

verdicts.reason: The evidence in E2 supports the claim that the knowledge gates are inspired by the powerful gate mechanism used in recurrent neural networks (RNN) to control information flow and are used to incorporate prior knowledge into the matching process.
The evidence in E2 supports the claim that the knowledge gates are used to filter out noise and highlight the useful information to matching in a piece of text.
The evidence in E4 supports the claim that the knowledge gates are located in the KEHNN architecture as shown in Figure 1.
The evidence in E5 supports the claim that the role of the knowledge gates in the KEHNN architecture is to incorporate prior knowledge and filter out noise, as shown in the zoomed view of Figure 1.
